classification.difficultyReason: Plot three points in different quadrants and find their images under a quarter-turn about the origin.

content.prompt: Plot the points given below on a number plane and rotate each one $90^\circ$ anticlockwise about the origin $O$. Write down the coordinates of each image point.

spec.description: Authored common number-plane drawing region for the explicitly requested plots; the source supplies no printed plane.
spec.mathematics: Unit grid with both axes spanning −5 to 5, sufficient for every original point and image.
spec.answerVisibility: No original points or image points are supplied in the student figure.

answer.worked: Plot $A(1,-2)$. A quarter-turn anticlockwise about the origin takes its position 1 unit right and 2 units down to 2 units right and 1 unit up. Therefore $A'(2,1)$.
Plot $B(1,4)$. A quarter-turn anticlockwise about the origin takes its position 1 unit right and 4 units up to 4 units left and 1 unit up. Therefore $B'(-4,1)$.
Plot $C(-2,1)$. A quarter-turn anticlockwise about the origin takes its position 2 units left and 1 unit up to 1 unit left and 2 units down. Therefore $C'(-1,-2)$.

spec.description: One complete common solution plane with all three original points and their labelled rotated images.
spec.mathematics: A(1,−2) rotates to A′(2,1); B(1,4) rotates to B′(−4,1); C(−2,1) rotates to C′(−1,−2). All rotations are 90° anticlockwise about (0,0).
spec.answerVisibility: All six plotted points and image labels appear only in answer editions.
